title: Hypercomplete comparison for a local equivalence of sites
statement:
A small Grothendieck site is a small category with specified covering sieves, containing the maximal sieve and closed under pullback of sieves and transitivity; a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. A family covers when its generated sieve covers. No fibre products in the underlying category are required. All sizes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced localization of cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and all higher composition data [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$-valued hypersheaf is a coherent presheaf $F$ such that for every hypercover $T_\bullet\to T$ the map $F(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(T_n)$ is an equivalence. Here a hypercover is an augmented simplicial family of representable presheaves whose maps to all matching presheaves are locally surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; $F$ on a family is the product of its values. Write $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ for the full enhanced category of such $F$ with $H^i(F(T))=0$ for every $T$ and $i<a$, for a fixed integer $a$. Morphisms are coherent natural transformations, and mapping complexes are the derived ends in the coherent presheaf category.

Let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor between small Grothendieck sites satisfying all of the following. It sends covering families to covering families. Every covering family of $p(C)$ can be refined by the image of a covering family of $C$. For each arrow $p(C')\to p(C)$ there is a covering $\{C'_i\to C'\}$ on which that arrow lifts to arrows $C'_i\to C$; and any two arrows with the same image under $p$ become equal on a covering of their source. Every object $D$ of $\mathcal D$ has a covering by arrows $p(C_i)\to D$.

Precomposition gives an equivalence of enhanced categories
$$p^*:\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal D,\Lambda)\simeq\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda).$$
A quasi-inverse is the homotopy right Kan extension, whose value at $D$ is $\operatorname{holim}_{(p(C)\to D)^{\mathrm{op}}}F(C)$, indexed by the opposite of the comma category of arrows $p(C)\to D$. It is a hypersheaf; the comparison is an equivalence on derived mapping complexes and is natural for commutative squares of these site functors. Both directions preserve the specified pointwise lower bound $a$. No full faithfulness of $p$ on its original hom-sets is required.

proof.text: Write $J,K$ for the two topologies and $p_!S$ for the image-generated sieve. Cover preservation gives $S\in J\Rightarrow p_!S\in K$. For the converse suppose $p_!S$ covers $p(C)$. Apply the cover-refinement hypothesis to the family of all its arrows to obtain a covering $\{t_i:C_i\to C\}$ with $p(t_i)=p(s_i)b_i$, where $s_i:A_i\to C$ belongs to $S$ and $b_i:p(C_i)\to p(A_i)$. Locally lift each $b_i$: on a covering $v_{ij}:C_{ij}\to C_i$ there are $c_{ij}:C_{ij}\to A_i$ with $p(c_{ij})=b_i p(v_{ij})$. The arrows $t_i v_{ij}$ and $s_i c_{ij}$ then have equal images. Local faithfulness supplies a further covering on which they are equal. Those composite covering arrows belong to $S$, so transitivity makes $S$ covering. Local fullness and local faithfulness also make the sieves $L_b,E_{f,g}$ in [lem-cbc-local-dense-ordinary-sheaves] cover on $\mathcal C$; cover preservation makes their image sieves cover on $\mathcal D$. Cover density is precisely the remaining hypothesis of that node. Thus all its sieve conditions hold without any fibre product.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-local-dense-ordinary-sheaves] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda}$; its small limits are compatible-family submodules of products. Write $L$ for restriction and $T$ for its right adjoint, whose underlying presheaf is ordinary Ran. By [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves], the fixed-$\Lambda$ module sheaves are additively equivalent to modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline\Lambda$, retaining the same abelian sheaves and maps. This lemma applies to our arbitrary covering-sieve topologies, without fibre products. Thus these are exactly the module-sheaf categories of [lem-cbc-bounded-below-hypersheaf-model]. The functor $L$ is additive sectionwise and $T$ by its limit formula. Now [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] gives exactness, injective preservation, and preservation of kernels and cokernels. Consequently termwise application commutes with cohomology sheaves: $\mathcal H^i(LM)=L\mathcal H^i(M)$ and $\mathcal H^i(TM)=T\mathcal H^i(M)$.

proof.text: Apply $L,T$ termwise to complexes. The ordinary unit $\mathrm{id}\to TL$ and counit $LT\to\mathrm{id}$ are then chain isomorphisms; their naturality for differentials is exactly the chain-map equation. Exactness from step 2 makes both functors preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. For a complex $A$ and a complex $I$, the additive adjunction identifies the product Hom complexes, with differential $dh=d_Ih-(-1)^{|h|}h d_A$, so the adjunction is dg. Its two composite isomorphisms and triangle equations are also dg. The enriched localization universal property [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] therefore gives mutually inverse enhanced derived functors $\mathbf L,\mathbf T$ and the localized coherent unit and counit. The cohomology calculation of step 2 shows that this equivalence restricts to cohomology sheaves zero below the specified $a$.

proof.text: Let $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ denote the derived-section equivalences of the current [lem-cbc-bounded-below-hypersheaf-model]. Its coherent-presheaf definition, derived mapping complexes and arbitrary covering-sieve sites are the ones in our statement, and its fixed bound $a$ is the same integer on both sites. The fixed-ring/constant-ring-sheaf identification of step 2 checks its module-category hypothesis. For a bounded-below derived sheaf object $M$ on $\mathcal D$, take a K-injective resolution $M\to I$ with injective terms by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The exact equivalence $L$ preserves K-injectivity: if $A$ is acyclic on $\mathcal C$, full faithfulness of the termwise dg equivalence $T$, followed by the inverse of $I\to TLI$, gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(A,LI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(TA,TLI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(TA,I)$, and $TA$ is acyclic. Thus $R\Gamma(C,LM)$ is represented by $(LI)(C)=I(p(C))$, which also represents $R\Gamma(p(C),M)$. The equality is natural in $C$, in chain maps, and in the full Hom complexes, since both evaluation maps act componentwise. Consequently $Q_{\mathcal C}\mathbf L\simeq p^*Q_{\mathcal D}$ as enhanced functors. The two $Q$'s and $\mathbf L$ are equivalences, so this proves that precomposition lands in hypersheaves and is an equivalence on the subcategories with bound $a$; its abstract quasi-inverse is $Q_{\mathcal D}\mathbf TQ_{\mathcal C}^{-1}$.

proof.text: We need a concrete model for coherent presheaves, before taking any comma limit. On the one-object category with only its identity and the topology in which just the maximal sieve covers, a sheaf of modules over the constant ring $\Lambda$ is simply a $\Lambda$-module. Apply [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model] to this small ringed site to obtain a stable combinatorial dg model for $\operatorname{Ch}(\Lambda)$ with quasi-isomorphisms as weak equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification] to the constant diagram with this value and identity Quillen transition functors, indexed by $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ for any small category $\mathcal E$. Strict sections are exactly complexes of module presheaves on $\mathcal E$, and objectwise weak equivalences are their quasi-isomorphisms, since kernels, images and cohomology of presheaves are computed objectwise [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], applied with the maximal-sieve topology. Thus their enhanced localization presents $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathbf D(\Lambda))$, including derived mapping complexes. This presentation identifies the localized restriction functor with coherent precomposition: on a strict diagram it restricts its objects, arrows and their strict composition diagrams, and the displayed coherent-end formula in the rectification statement restricts by selecting strings in the smaller index category. The localization universal property [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] then identifies these functors and their specified comparisons after inversion.

source.place: Constant-diagram case of the existing Quillen-section rectification and trivial one-object site case of the existing flat model; agent-written application for the dense-site comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-kinjective-derived-mapping-complex] to the module and module-presheaf categories in the stable presentation of step 5: use the one-object identity category for modules, and $E=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ for presheaves on a small category $\mathcal E$. Its product Hom differential is exactly $dh=d_Jh-(-1)^{|h|}h d_A$. Hence for every complex $A$ and K-injective $J$, this full Hom complex computes the derived mapping complex, naturally in both variables. The cited statement includes inversion of source quasi-isomorphisms and of quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective targets, and compatibility with composition and its coherent localization. We use this all-degree comparison in the two explicit dg adjunctions below; no enhanced assertion is inferred from a degree-zero Hom bijection alone.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, (1) implies (3), is the ordinary all-shifts input. proof.text:
Let $F\simeq Q_{\mathcal C}N$ be a hypersheaf with the specified bound. Choose a K-injective resolution $N\to J$ with injective terms by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $i$ for inclusion of module sheaves into presheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], its left adjoint $\#$ is exact. The degreewise adjunction is an isomorphism of Hom complexes: its naturality with respect to the two differentials gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(A,iJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\#A,J).$$
For acyclic $A$, $\#A$ is acyclic, so $iJ$ is K-injective as a presheaf complex. The derived-section model [lem-cbc-bounded-below-hypersheaf-model] says that its coherent value presheaf represents $F$: at $C$ its value is $J(C)$ computing $R\Gamma(C,N)$. For an acyclic sheaf complex $B$ on $\mathcal D$, the dg adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,TJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(LB,J)$, which is acyclic because $L$ is exact. Thus $TJ$ is K-injective; it has injective terms by step 2. For an acyclic presheaf complex $A$ on $\mathcal D$, $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(A,iTJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\#A,TJ)$ is acyclic because $\#$ is exact. Consequently $i(TJ)$ is K-injective as a presheaf complex and represents $Q_{\mathcal D}\mathbf T N$.

source.place: Agent-written enriched derived Kan calculation; ordinary prototypes Stacks Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, and Tag 03A0, lemma-equivalence

proof.text:
Construct the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $R^0_p$. For a complex $V$ of presheaves on $\mathcal C$, its degree-$r$ value at $D$ is the submodule of $\prod_{(C,f:p(C)\to D)}V^r(C)$ consisting of families $(x_{C,f})$ satisfying $V(h)x_{C,f}=x_{C',f p(h)}$ for each $h:C'\to C$. Differential is coordinatewise, and restriction along $b:D'\to D$ selects the coordinates $(C,bf')$ for $f':p(C)\to D'$. This constructs the small comma limit, including the empty case, without any final-object assertion. A map $\alpha:p^*G\to V$ gives $G\to R^0_p V$ by $g\mapsto(\alpha_C(G(f)g))_{C,f}$; the inverse sends $\beta:G\to R^0_p V$ to its coordinate $(C,\mathrm{id}_{p(C)})$ after evaluating at $p(C)$. The compatibility equations show these formulas are inverse. Applying them in every Hom degree gives the dg adjunction
$$\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(G,R^0_p V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(p^*G,V);$$
the Hom differential commutes because the two formulas are natural in both complexes. Since $p^*$ is exact objectwise, this adjunction shows that $R^0_p V$ is K-injective whenever $V$ is: for acyclic $A$, its Hom complex is $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(p^*A,V)$, which is acyclic. By step 6, for K-injective $V$ this actual dg adjunction is therefore an equivalence of the derived mapping complexes. For $V=iJ$, the ordinary comparison theorem [lem-cbc-local-dense-ordinary-sheaves] identifies $R^0_p(iJ)=i(TJ)$ termwise, so it already represents the abstract inverse found in step 4.

source.place: Tag 03A0 ordinary right Kan limit formula; explicit compatible-family adjunction. No use of the incorrect final-object sentence in its proof

proof.text:
To prove that this ordinary limit on the chosen representative is the required homotopy limit, fix $D$ and put $E=(p\downarrow D)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $q:E\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ the projection. Regard a module diagram $V$ on $E$ as a presheaf on $E^{\mathrm{op}}$. Presheaf diagram categories are abelian with objectwise cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], applied with maximal-sieve topologies on $\mathcal C$ and $E^{\mathrm{op}}$. The restriction $q^*$ has an exact left adjoint $q_!$ given explicitly by
$$(q_!V)(C)=\bigoplus_{f:p(C)\to D}V(C,f).$$
For $h:C'\to C$ each summand indexed by $f$ maps to the summand indexed by $fp(h)$ using the corresponding arrow $(C,f)\to(C',fp(h))$ of $E$. A map from these direct sums to a presheaf $A$ is exactly a compatible family of maps $V(C,f)\to A(C)$, proving $q_!\dashv q^*$, also on Hom complexes. Exactness is objectwise: kernels are componentwise in a direct sum, and a finite-support vector in the target of a surjection lifts by lifting its finitely many nonzero coordinates; hence direct sums preserve short exact sequences. Thus for acyclic $B$, $q_!B$ is acyclic, and
$$\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,q^*iJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(q_!B,iJ)$$
is acyclic. In degree zero this says that every map from an acyclic complex to $q^*iJ$ is null-homotopic, which is the K-injective condition in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Thus $q^*iJ$ is K-injective in the comma diagram category. The argument uses the actual source arrows in the comma category, not local fullness or a purported final object.

source.place: Agent explicit direct-sum left adjoint for the comma projection and its exactness; ordinary comma indexing from Tag 03A0

proof.text:
For any small $E$, the constant-diagram functor $\Delta:\operatorname{Ch}(\Lambda)\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Fun}(E,\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda}))$ is exact. Its right adjoint is the limit, constructed as the compatible-family subcomplex of the product. Explicitly, a degree-$r$ map $B\to\lim_E V$ is a family of degree-$r$ maps $b_e:B\to V(e)$ such that $V(\alpha)b_e=b_{e'}$ for each $\alpha:e\to e'$. These are exactly the degree-$r$ maps $\Delta B\to V$. Projection and tuple formation are inverse and commute with $dh=d_Vh-(-1)^r h d_B$, proving the dg adjunction. Thus $\lim_E q^*iJ$ is a K-injective $\Lambda$-complex: Hom from an acyclic $B$ is $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\Delta B,q^*iJ)$, acyclic by step 9. Step 6 on both sides of this dg adjunction gives, naturally in every $B\in\mathbf D(\Lambda)$,
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda}(B,\lim_E q^*iJ)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(E),\mathbf D(\Lambda))}(\Delta B,q^*F).$$
Here step 5 supplies the coherent-diagram identification for the small category $E^{\mathrm{op}}$. This equivalence is induced by the actual projection cone from the constructed limit. Passing to underlying mapping spaces and applying the cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that this cone is limiting. Hence
$$(iTJ)(D)=(R^0_piJ)(D)=\lim_E q^*iJ\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{(p(C)\to D)^{\mathrm{op}}}F(C).$$
The cone projections, their dg adjunction, and the canonical mapping comparisons in step 6 are natural in $D$ and in maps of representatives. Their localization is therefore an enhanced natural comparison [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], not unrelated objectwise choices. This proves the homotopy right Kan formula and its hypersheaf property, since $iTJ$ already represents $Q_{\mathcal D}\mathbf TN$ by step 7.

source.place: Agent proof of the homotopy-limit universal property via the exact constant-diagram adjunction, the all-degree K-injective mapping comparison of Tag 070I, and the existing coherent cone criterion

proof.text: The unit and counit on these representatives are the maps constructed in step 8. In particular the counit $p^*R_pF\to F$ is evaluation at $(C,\mathrm{id}_{p(C)})$, whereas the unit $G\to R_pp^*G$ has cone maps $G(D)\to G(p(C))$ induced by $p(C)\to D$. For the first triangle, $g\in G(p(C))$ is sent by the unit to the family $(G(f)g)_{A,f:p(A)\to p(C)}$, and evaluation at $(C,\mathrm{id})$ returns $g$. For the second triangle, a compatible family $(x_{C,f})$ is first sent at $(A,b:p(A)\to D)$ to the restricted family $(x_{C,bf})$ and the right Kan extension of the counit then selects $x_{A,b}$. Thus both triangle composites are identities before localization. Under steps 4 and 7--10 these are the localized unit and counit of the exact sheaf equivalence $L\dashv T$, hence both are equivalences. Their naturality and triangle diagrams localize with all their coherences by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. On derived mapping complexes the inverse of restriction sends $h:p^*G\to p^*H$ to $\eta_H^{-1}R_p(h)\eta_G$. Unit naturality gives $\eta_H^{-1}R_p(p^*f)\eta_G=f$. For an arbitrary $h$, the triangles identify $(p^*\eta_H)^{-1}$ and $(p^*\eta_G)^{-1}$ with the corresponding counits; counit naturality then gives $p^*(\eta_H^{-1}R_p(h)\eta_G)=\epsilon_{p^*H}p^*R_p(h)\epsilon_{p^*G}^{-1}=h$. In a composite the adjacent factors $\eta_H\eta_H^{-1}$ cancel, and identities remain identities, proving compatibility with composition on the full mapping complexes. This also follows from the explicit derived Hom-complex adjunction of step 8; no conclusion about derived ends is taken just from ordinary local fullness.

proof.text: Restriction preserves the pointwise bound by evaluation. Its inverse preserves it by steps 7--10: under the bounded-below hypersheaf model it is the exact sheaf equivalence $\mathbf T$, whose cohomology sheaves remain zero below $a$, and the stated equivalence $\mathbf D_{\ge a}\simeq\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}$ then gives pointwise vanishing. This uses the model's explicit subcategory with the fixed bound, rather than any assertion that ordinary evaluation of sheaves is exact.

source.place: Tag 03A0, lemma-equivalence, ordinary comparison prototype. Agent-written enhanced proof through existing bounded-below hypersheaf realization and generic derived presheaf Kan extension; no enhanced assertion is attributed to this Stacks tag.

proof.text:
For a commutative square $pu=vp'$ of the site functors in the statement, with $u:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal C$, $v:\mathcal D'\to\mathcal D$ and $p':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$, coherent precomposition gives $p'^*v^*=u^*p^*$ on coherent presheaves. Since $u$ and $v$ satisfy the hypotheses of the statement, step 4 applied to them shows that $u^*$ and $v^*$ carry hypersheaves to hypersheaves, and they preserve the pointwise bound $a$ by evaluation (step 12); so the identity is one of functors between the $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}$ categories. By steps 4 and 11 the horizontal pairs $p^*\dashv R_p$ and $p'^*\dashv R_{p'}$ are enhanced adjoint equivalences with the constructed units and counits. Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-equivalence-square-mates] with $L=p^*$, $R=R_p$, $L'=p'^*$, $R'=R_{p'}$, $U=u^*$, $V=v^*$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Its specified mate is exactly
$$v^*R_p\xrightarrow{\eta^{p'}}R_{p'}p'^*v^*R_p=R_{p'}u^*p^*R_p\xrightarrow{R_{p'}u^*\epsilon^p}R_{p'}u^*.$$
The cited mate theorem makes it an equivalence and supplies the identity, pasting and all higher coherence compatibilities through the contractible space of counit-compatible lifts. This proves the asserted naturality of the hypersheaf comparison, without claiming a base-change theorem for arbitrary comma-category Kan extensions.
